subject: Baseline IO pricing per 1M tokens + supported model families
messages:
From: Samir Patel <samir@emberhealth.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 17 Jul 2028 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Quick ask — per-1M token IO rates + supported models

Hi Irene,

Thanks for taking a look — small intro: I'm Samir on the AI product team at Ember Health. We're evaluating hosted providers for an outpatient triage assistant (mainly short-context chat + structured output) and want a baseline per-1M token cost to feed into our ROI model. A couple quick asks: 

- Can you share standard input/output per-1M token rates for hosted API (no commitment) and any note on how you count tokens (input vs output split)?
- Which model families are available on the hosted tier today (small/mid/large) and any recommended ones for short chat (<=512 tokens)?
- If we can share our current monthly token estimate (~30M total; ~70% outputs after generation), do you have a ballpark for volume discount thresholds or simple committed tiers we should consider?

Would appreciate a short reply or a one-pager we can share with finance. Attaching a coarse usage CSV from our side.

Best,
Samir
Samir Patel
Product Manager, Ember Health
Attachment: ember_usage_snapshot_q2.csv (50 KB)
From: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>

Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 17 Jul 2028 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Quick ask — per-1M token IO rates + supported models

Hi Samir — thanks for the details and the CSV. Looping in Aditya (account lead) and Marissa (pricing/solutions) so we can give a concise baseline and next steps.

Quick baseline to start the conversation (hosted API, list pricing, USD):
- Input tokens: $0.80 per 1M tokens
- Output tokens: $1.60 per 1M tokens
- Recommended short-chat models: redwood-small-v2, redwood-medium-v1, and the redwood-chat-512 optimized family (latency-friendly for <=512 tokens).

Notes:
- Our hosted counts input and output separately; you will see separate line items in billing.
- The redwood-chat-512 family is tuned for low latency and lower token-cost per inference due to prompt-packing optimizations.
- For reference, 30M tokens/month (70% output) with list pricing comes out to a simple estimate: 9M input tokens and 21M output tokens => ~$ (9 * 0.8 + 21 * 1.6) per 1M multiples — we can put a cleaned calculator in a PDF.

Aditya / Marissa — can you confirm any current promotional or commitment tiers that would materially change the unit economics for a 12-month commit at ~30M/mo?

Irene
Irene Choi
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

Samir — thanks for the extra context. A couple clarifying Qs before we finalize a short quote: 
- Is the 30M/month an expected steady state or a peak estimate during pilot?
- When you say 70% outputs, is that averaged over sessions? Are there heavy multi-turn flows where outputs are short (e.g., 2-3 tokens) or long (200+ tokens)?

Ballpark committed pricing we can offer for a 12-month term (subject to SOW/contract):
- Input: $0.60 per 1M tokens
- Output: $1.10 per 1M tokens
- Requirements: 80% usage of specified model family (redwood-chat-512 or redwood-medium-v1) and minimum 12-month commit at 30M/mo.

I attached a short PDF with the calculator and the conservative cost estimate for your finance team. If you prefer, we can do a short 20-minute call tomorrow to walk through numbers and model recommendations.

Aditya
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Thanks — helpful. A couple quick follow-ups: 
- The 30M is our conservative steady-state projection after pilot. Peak can hit ~45M for short windows.
- Outputs are usually medium length (avg ~120 tokens) with occasional long summaries. Sessions average 6 turns (so there is some KV/cache benefit we hope for).

Two asks: can you confirm whether the committed pricing above assumes prefix/KV caching enabled (i.e., does Redwood apply any additional discounts for KV cache or batching optimizations)? And can you send the short 20-min slot — tomorrow afternoon PT works for us.

If we get terms similar to your committed numbers and caching is enabled by default for the chat model, Ember is ready to move to a short PO for Q4 planning.

Samir
